svg.text: Each number = sum of the two above; row n hides the coefficients of (a + b)ⁿ
Symmetry: the triangle is mirror-symmetric — C(n,k) = C(n, n−k)
Each entry C(n,k) = n!/(k!(n−k)!) counts the ways to pick k things from n
Blaise Pascal published it in 1654 — but Pingala (India), Al-Karaji (Persia) and Yang Hui (China) knew it earlier
Uses: expanding binomials, probability coin flips, combinatorics identity checks
